gaps:
Every decade from 1e33 to 1e47 J now has a rung inside it, and no step between neighbouring rungs is over 20x. Under the combined rule (at most about 10x the rung below, or at least about 10% of the rung above), every energy from 2.5e32 J to about 5e48 J gets a valid comparison. Spans where the multiple of the rung below would exceed 10x, so the page must use a share of the rung above instead:
(1) Earth's binding energy (2.49e32 J) to Earth's orbital motion (2.65e33 J): 10.6x. This is at the edge of the band, shared with the planetary topic.
(2) The Sun's year (1.21e34 J) to Jupiter's orbital motion (1.62e35 J): 13.4x, so 1.2e35 to 1.6e35 J.
(3) The nova (1e38 J) to the 2004 magnetar flare (2e39 J): 20x, so 1e39 to 2e39 J. Both rungs are rough, so this part of the 1e39 decade has no firm rung. The Moon turned into energy (6.6e39 J) is the nearest firm one.
(4) A supernova's light (1e42 J) to the Sun's output for a billion years (1.21e43 J): 12.1x.
(5) Jupiter turned into energy (1.71e44 J) to SN 1998bw (3e45 J): 17.6x, so 1.7e45 to 3e45 J. SN 1998bw is disputed by about 15x. If it is dropped, the step from Jupiter's mass-energy to a supernova's total energy (3e46 J) is 176x, beyond the 100x maximum, and the 1e45 decade has no rung.
Above the top rung (GW150914, 5.4e47 J), the 1e48 decade has no rung. Energies above about 5e48 J are beyond the ladder.
